method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet' (published 29 November 2018), 23 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC6745959). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Australian Prescriber Editorial Executive Committee, Aust Prescr 45(6):213 (doi 10.18773/austprescr.2022.071) 'Decitabine/cedazuridine for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndromes (new drug comment)' (published 12 October 2022), 6 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC9722354). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps the EHA/ELN 2018 claims (S1) unchanged and adds Australian Prescriber's 2022 new-drug comment on oral decitabine–cedazuridine (S2, PMC9722354), which S1 predates. S2 is a drug commentary, not a guideline, and its trial data pool CMML with MDS.

claims.claim: **CMML is the commonest myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm (about 1/100,000 a year)** and ranges from MDS-like disease with monocytosis to highly proliferative disease with high white counts, splenomegaly and extramedullary involvement.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classify by WHO 2016 blast counts:** CMML-0 (<2% blood, <5% marrow), CMML-1 (2–4% blood and/or 5–9% marrow), CMML-2 (5–19% blood, 10–19% marrow, or Auer rods). The grade carries prognostic weight. (Level D)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also split dysplastic from proliferative CMML at a white count of 13:** they behave and are managed differently (cytopenias versus organomegaly, leucocytosis and constitutional symptoms).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for organomegaly; measure a suspected enlarged spleen** (e.g. ultrasound). Serous effusions and skin infiltration signal worse prognosis.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Survival varies from over 50 months to under a year,** so every patient needs risk stratification with a CMML-specific model that uses mutations (GFM, CPSS-mol or Mayo Molecular); without mutation data, use CPSS or the MD Anderson score. (Level D)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adverse markers:** complex karyotype and chromosome 7 abnormalities; ASXL1 mutation (consistently shorter survival); RUNX1, NRAS and SETBP1 mutations; more mutations overall.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weigh the patient as well as the disease:** age (median about 77), performance status, comorbidity, frailty, nutrition, cognition and quality of life. Scores were built in patients around 70 or older, so use caution in younger people.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor with full blood count and differential, spleen size and extramedullary disease, and a standard symptom score (e.g. MPN-SAF).** Repeat the marrow with cytogenetics if these change.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First decide whether the patient could have an allogeneic transplant.**
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Watch and wait** when there is no marrow blast excess and no (or only mild, asymptomatic) cytopenia or major myeloproliferation. Treatment usually starts for Hb under 10 g/dL, platelets under 30 or bleeding, symptomatic splenomegaly, other extramedullary disease or constitutional symptoms. (Level D)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Allogeneic transplant is the only cure.** Recommended under age 70 for higher-risk disease with a donor and no major contraindication; consider it in selected lower-risk patients with severe cytopenias or poor-risk mutations (ASXL1, RUNX1, SETBP1, NRAS). (Level B)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before transplant, CMML-2 is usually debulked.** Intensive chemotherapy suits fit patients with high disease burden; a hypomethylating agent suits unfit patients or bridges while a donor is found.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intensive chemotherapy is otherwise not recommended** (chemoresistant disease, short remissions), except as a bridge to transplant in CMML-2 or when disease borders on AML (Auer rods, NPM1 mutation). (Level D)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Azacitidine for transplant-ineligible dysplastic CMML with more than 10% marrow blasts** (Level B). Consider it, ideally in a trial, for blasts above 5% with significant cytopenias or myeloproliferation (Level D).
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypomethylating agents give about 50% overall and 25% complete response, with median survival around 20 months;** there is no basis for choosing azacitidine over decitabine. Grade 3–4 blood toxicity occurs in 15% to 55%.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After hypomethylating-agent failure the outlook is poor** (median survival about 7 months; half transform to AML), and switching azacitidine to decitabine does not seem to help.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hydroxyurea for proliferative CMML without major cytopenias or blast excess** (Level A): 1 g/day beat etoposide 150 mg/week (median survival 20 vs 9 months). Start on symptoms and comorbidity, not a set count; taper or stop if transfusion needs rise.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Decitabine–cedazuridine (Inqovi, 35 mg/100 mg tablets) is approved in Australia for CMML and myelodysplastic syndromes.** It is an oral alternative to hypomethylating agents otherwise given by infusion on several consecutive days each month: cedazuridine blocks the cytidine deaminase in gut and liver that would otherwise break down oral decitabine.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber Editorial Executive Committee, Aust Prescr 45(6):213 (doi 10.18773/austprescr.2022.071), 'Decitabine/cedazuridine for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndromes (new drug comment)', published 12 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9722354/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Oral 35 mg decitabine with 100 mg cedazuridine gave 97.6% of the decitabine exposure (AUC) of 20 mg/m2 intravenously;** the phase III crossover also found similar exposure.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber Editorial Executive Committee, Aust Prescr 45(6):213 (doi 10.18773/austprescr.2022.071), 'Decitabine/cedazuridine for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndromes (new drug comment)', published 12 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9722354/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Take it fasting, since food reduces decitabine absorption, and keep drugs that raise gastric pH at least four hours away.** No dose change is advised for mild hepatic or mild to moderate renal impairment; more severe impairment has not been studied.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber Editorial Executive Committee, Aust Prescr 45(6):213 (doi 10.18773/austprescr.2022.071), 'Decitabine/cedazuridine for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndromes (new drug comment)', published 12 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9722354/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Efficacy (CMML and MDS together):** in the phase II trial (80 patients; five-day cycles every 28 days, median seven cycles) 60% responded, 21% completely, with complete responses lasting a median 13.3 months and median overall survival 18.3 months. Interim phase III data (133 patients) also showed 21% complete responses, and some patients stopped needing transfusions.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber Editorial Executive Committee, Aust Prescr 45(6):213 (doi 10.18773/austprescr.2022.071), 'Decitabine/cedazuridine for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndromes (new drug comment)', published 12 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9722354/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Most patients have serious adverse effects, chiefly neutropenia, anaemia and thrombocytopenia with bleeding risk.** Check blood counts regularly and delay or reduce doses for abnormal results; rises in creatinine or liver enzymes may also need dose changes. Fatigue, nausea, dizziness, diarrhoea and constipation are common; five of 80 phase II patients stopped for adverse effects.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber Editorial Executive Committee, Aust Prescr 45(6):213 (doi 10.18773/austprescr.2022.071), 'Decitabine/cedazuridine for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndromes (new drug comment)', published 12 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9722354/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **It is easier to give than azacitidine, but whether outcomes are comparable is not yet known** (awaiting full phase III results).
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber Editorial Executive Committee, Aust Prescr 45(6):213 (doi 10.18773/austprescr.2022.071), 'Decitabine/cedazuridine for chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndromes (new drug comment)', published 12 October 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9722354/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **ESAs for symptomatic anaemia in lower-risk disease with low serum EPO** (Level B); erythroid response was 64%, lasting a median 7 months.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **G-CSF:** no data support its safe use for azacitidine-induced neutropenia, though it may be tried in febrile patients not responding to antibiotics. Drug-induced severe neutropenia is managed by tapering or pausing the drug.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfuse red cells on symptoms, not a fixed number;** Hb below 80 g/L is usually symptomatic. Rising transfusion needs should prompt a search for hypersplenism, bleeding, haemolysis or progression. (Level D)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Iron chelation may be considered** in transfusion-dependent lower-risk patients with ferritin above 1000 ng/mL after about 25 units, if life expectancy is not otherwise under 3 years. (Level D)
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Isolated severe thrombocytopenia without anaemia or blast excess suggests an immune component:** a short steroid course may help (Level D). Thrombopoietin agonists are not recommended outside trials.
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer clinical trials at every stage.**
claims.locator: European Hematology Association (EHA) and European LeukemiaNet (ELN), HemaSphere 2018;2(6):e150, 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemias in Adults: Recommendations From the European Hematology Association and the European LeukemiaNet', published 29 November 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6745959/, retrieved 2026-09-23
